title: Connectivity pipeline
description: Monnit push → inbound → Kafka → landing → event jobs → delivery to monitor-server. Panels follow the alert rules in monitor-platform docs/connectivity/hardening-plan.md (Phase 2).

panels.title: Landed, 15 min
panels.description: New facts landed by the flows worker. Zero for 15 min is the landing-silent alert.

panels.title: Jobs pending
panels.description: Rows waiting for a delivery slice to claim them. A steady few is normal; a growing count with no attempts means no slice serves them.

panels.title: Oldest job
panels.description: Age of the oldest pending/failed/processing job. delivery-stuck warns at 1 h, pages at 4 h.

panels.title: Jobs dead
panels.description: Rejected by the target or retries exhausted. The job-dead alert; Event jobs → Subjects → head.

panels.title: Kafka lag
panels.description: Records the landing group has not consumed yet, worst partition. landing-lag warns at 1000 for 10 min.

panels.title: Shards down
panels.description: Shard hosts or performers not running. The Shard phases table below names them.

panels.title: Requests by status
panels.description: Monnit pushes answered by the edge. 202 accepted; 4xx the sender's fault; 503 Kafka unreachable (inbound-503).

panels.title: 503s, last hour
panels.description: Pushes refused because Kafka was unreachable. Nothing to replay here: confirm with Monnit whether the window was retried.

panels.title: Inbound up
panels.description: Instances whose metrics reached the collector in the last minutes. The inbound-unhealthy alert is this going to 0 for 10 min.

panels.title: Events landed / min
panels.description: New domain events written by the land flow (resends are not counted).

panels.title: Items by result / min
panels.description: Every item a batch settled: done = landed, duplicate = already seen, the rest carry a reason (dead letters).

panels.title: Batch duration p95 by flow
panels.description: Take-to-settle time per batch.

panels.title: Batch failures / min
panels.description: Batch-level failures by stage. Transient ones retry; the rest pause the work lane after the policy's limit.

panels.title: Shard phases
panels.description: Current host phase of every work lane. paused: read the reason in the Flows sheet; fatal: the consumer crashed.

panels.title: Kafka consumer lag by partition
panels.description: High watermark minus committed offset per partition of the landing group.

panels.title: Attempts by outcome / min
panels.description: Calls to monitor-server: delivered; retry (5xx/timeout, backoff); defer (401/403, the delivery-unauthorized alert); reject (other 4xx, job dead); threw (no response).

panels.title: In vs out / min
panels.description: Jobs created by the land flow against jobs delivered. Out below in for long is a growing backlog.

panels.title: Backlog by status
panels.description: Unfinished rows per status; processed is left out because it only grows.

panels.title: Oldest unfinished job age
panels.description: The delivery-stuck signal with its two thresholds drawn.

panels.title: Delivery duration
panels.description: Time for one call to monitor-server to settle.

panels.title: Deployed versions
panels.description: service_version is the commit sha stamped by the ECS task definition. One row per service that is exporting right now.

panels.title: Collector
panels.description: Prometheus scraping the collector's own telemetry. The collector-silent alert.

panels.title: Exporter queue
panels.description: Single replica, no persistent queue: a filling queue means Prometheus or Tempo is not keeping up and points will be dropped.

panels.title: Metric points / s
panels.description: OTLP metric points the collector accepted vs refused from the three services.

panels.title: Services up
panels.description: Connectivity services whose metrics reached Prometheus recently; three when inbound, flows worker and outbound all export.

panels.title: Collector uptime
panels.description: Seconds since the collector process started. A reset means a restart, and with no persistent queue, a gap in every series.
